text:
A: Hi! Can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah, fine. Gareth.
A: Ollie. Nice to meet you. Last one, I think?
B: I think so, yeah.
A: So what do you do, Gareth?
B: Quantity surveyor. Commercial manager at a contractor in Birmingham. Hospitals and schools.
A: Oh, no way. My dad's a chartered surveyor. He's in the City, though, sort of property side.
B: Right. RICS?
A: Yeah, I think so. He's got the certificate in the hallway. Bit like yours, actually.
B: Ha. Firm paid for mine. I made sure they did.
A: That's smart. And what do you do day to day? I've genuinely never fully understood what my dad does.
B: Er, cost reports, valuations every month, subcontractor accounts. Making sure the job doesn't lose money. Lot of spreadsheets.
A: I quite like a spreadsheet, honestly. I'm the one in the house who made the cleaning rota. Laminated it.
B: Laminated. Good lad. Does anyone stick to it?
A: No. Absolutely not. The War Studies guy hasn't done the bins since October.
B: There's always one. Same on site.
A: I'm a student, by the way, second year at King's, geography. I'm applying for transport planning internships, TfL, Arup, AECOM. Do you work with any of them?
B: Not directly. We come across the big consultancies on public sector jobs. They're decent. Graduate schemes are competitive, though, so get your applications in early.
A: Yeah, I've got a calendar of deadlines. Slightly obsessive.
B: Nothing wrong with that. Most people don't.
A: Do you do much outside work?
B: Golf on Saturdays. Running twice a week. 5k, six in the morning, same route.
A: Oh nice, what sort of time?
B: Twenty-six, twenty-seven. I'm not trying to win anything. It's for the weight, mainly.
A: That's solid, though, at six in the morning. I do parkrun most Saturdays, Burgess Park. I got nineteen forty a few weeks ago, which I'm, yeah, still a bit smug about.
B: That's quick.
A: Thanks. I'm thinking about the marathon ballot, but I feel like I'll regret it at mile twenty.
B: Probably. My lad's called Oliver, funnily enough. He's eleven. Football and swimming.
A: Oh, good name. Is he any good?
B: He's alright at the football. Swimming, he needs to try harder. More bothered about his grades, to be honest. That's what matters.
A: Ha, my dad used to say that. Football?
B: Blues. You?
A: Watford. So, you know. Suffering.
B: We're both suffering, then.
A: Yeah, pretty much. So with the QS stuff, did you always know that's what you—
